newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 20. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - May 20. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories in its Tuesday edition:
* The Dow Industrials tumbled in the morning, but recovered later in the day, ending up modestly.
* E.W. Scripps Co has agreed to buy the media properties of Harte-Hanks Communications Inc for $605 million.
* Esquire editor Edward Kosner is leaving the magazine.
* Delgratia Mining Corp said there is "insignificant gold" at its site in Nevada and is seeking a criminal investigation into possible tampering of ore samples.
* Limited Inc reported an 11 percent drop in operating earnings while Toys R Us Inc posted a 57 percent gain.
* A Harvard University study shows that exposure to second-hand smoke doubles a person's risk of heart disease.
* Federal antitrust officials said that internal company documents held by Staples Inc and Office Depot Inc bolsters their argument that a merged company would lead to increased prices.
* The United States and its major trading partners remain divided over how to enact and enforce a global ban on commercial bribery.
* Sun Microsystems Inc said it plans to sell encryption software created by a Russian company to international customers.

* Mobil Corp said it is in talks with several companies to possibly link its refining and marketing operations. It would not comment on a report it was discussing a merger of those businesses with Amoco Corp.
* ONYX Pharmaceuticals Inc has reported promising results in an early trial of its treatment for cancers of the head and neck.
* Golf sensation Tiger Woods has signed a five-year contract to be a spokesman for American Express Co..

* HSN Inc (corrects from Home Shopping Network Inc) plans to acquire a 47.5 percent stake in Ticketmaster Group Inc from Paul Allen, a co-founder of Microsoft Corp, and additional 2.5 percent stake on the open market.
* The Justice Department has issued a formal request seeking internal documents from Microsoft Corp on its planned $425 million purchase of WebTV Networks Inc.
* Across the U.S., prestigious teaching hospitals are turning to mergers and alliances as a result of cost-cutting measures imposed by managed care companies and government agencies.
